narrative:
With complete feeds, reconciled balances and eliminations posted, the October management P&L builds itself from governed data. Revenue is NOK 499M and gross profit NOK 180M, a 36.1% gross margin against a 36.8% budget. Contribution is NOK 29M after store and channel opex.

Intersport (37.9%) and Sport 1 (37.5%) are close to budget. Anton Sport leads at 40.0% on lifestyle footwear. E-commerce trails at 24.3% because it carries full parcel freight even when Intersport stores pick and hand over the order.

Two of the agent adjustments make the P&L more honest rather than better looking: a markdown reserve on aged summer stock now, and moving supplier marketing contributions into COGS where the trading terms say they belong.

signals.title: Aged summer stock in franchise stores
signals.excerpt: NOK 9.8M of summer outdoor stock is older than 180 days. Markdown timing affects both group and store-owner margins.

signals.title: Winter season build — inbound plan
signals.excerpt: Alpine, cross-country and outerwear inbound peaks in October ahead of November and December trading. GRNI and rebate accruals are largest in this window.

signals.title: Leadership business case — data platform
signals.excerpt: A 10-slide leadership deck is being prepared to justify modernising the data platform. Month-end close reliability is the lead argument.
